test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: For what purpose are pins and clips used in engineering drawings?

options.text: To transfer dimensions and dividing lines into a number of equal parts
To draw horizontal lines, parallel lines and to guide/hold the set squares
To fasten the drawing sheet on to the drawing board firmly so that it does not shake
To support the drawing paper/tracing paper for making drawing

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Purpose of Pins and Clips in Engineering Drawings:**

**Definition:** Pins and clips are essential tools used in engineering drawings for holding the drawing sheets securely onto the drawing board. They ensure that the sheets remain stable and do not move or shake during the drawing process, thereby maintaining accuracy and precision in the design work.

**Function:** When preparing engineering drawings, the drawing sheet needs to remain firmly in place on the drawing board. Pins and clips are employed to fasten the sheet securely to prevent unnecessary movement, which could lead to errors in the drawings. This stability is particularly important when intricate designs or precise measurements are involved.

**Advantages:**

 
• Ensures stability of the drawing sheet, preventing movement or shaking during the drawing process.
 
• Improves accuracy and precision in engineering drawings by maintaining the sheet's alignment.
 
• Facilitates ease of drawing, as the user does not have to constantly adjust the position of the sheet.
 
• Provides a simple and effective solution for securing the sheet without damaging it.
